//limits: 0 = unlimited, overriding config:recommended's prHourlyLimit 2 / prConcurrentLimit 10. Every available update opens a PR immediately rather than queueing in the dashboard's Rate-Limited section. Opening a PR is not deploying -- ArgoCD only acts on what lands on main -- so the cost of this is PR noise and CI minutes, not risk.

customManagers.description: Bump pinned upstream YAML release URLs (e.g. Gateway API CRDs)

packageRules.description: apps/archive/** is not deployed. The AppSet generators only scan apps/system/*/* and apps/homelab/* (see appsets/), so nothing under archive/ ever reaches the cluster. Renovate was opening PRs for ~6 dead apps.
Homelab container images: grouped. Blast radius is one stateless app each, so an all-or-nothing PR is fine and keeps the queue short.
Homelab Helm charts: grouped, same reasoning.

System charts + the root ArgoCD chart get ONE PR PER DEPENDENCY. No groupName is set for these, and that absence is what splits them. These can take the cluster down (cilium = CNI, longhorn = data, argo-cd = the thing doing the deploying), so each needs its own reviewable diff and its own revert. separateMinorPatch additionally splits e.g. a cert-manager patch from a cert-manager minor.
Let a release sit before offering it, so yanked or immediately-hotfixed releases never reach a PR.
